indicator_assessments.name: Hyperscaler CapEx plateau (rate stabilizes)
indicator_assessments.description: Hyperscalers keep spending at enormous scale but STOP ACCELERATING — next-period guidance lands flat vs the prior baseline. This is the 'infrastructure is built' moment: a peak-confirmation signal, distinct from CapEx acceleration (t2_capex_parabolic, boom fuel) and from CapEx cuts (Tier 4, bust confirmation).
indicator_assessments.what_to_look_for: A tracked hyperscaler (MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META) guides next-period CapEx FLAT vs its prior baseline (within ±5%) or uses stabilization language: 'stabilize', 'similar level', 'in line with', 'discipline', 'ROI focus', 'moderating growth rate'. STATUS LADDER: 1 hyperscaler at plateau = Partially fired; 2 or more = Fired. CANONICAL EXAMPLE (2026-07-30): Microsoft guiding FY27 CapEx at $190B against a $190B 2026 baseline = plateau, Partially fired. HARD RULES: (1) This is NOT CapEx cutting — dollars remain enormous; the SIGNAL is the growth rate reaching zero. An explicit guide-DOWN >5% hands off to the Tier 4 cut/idling family — and this signal REMAINS fired (progression continues, it does not reverse). (2) Guidance still growing >5% YoY is NOT this signal, however 'disciplined' the language — that is decelerating acceleration, still t2_capex_parabolic territory. (3) This is a CONTRARIAN-DIRECTION peak indicator: a plateau is LATE-CYCLE CONFIRMATION ('we are done building — thanks Nvidia, Micron, SK Hynix'), never good news for memory suppliers, never a reversal of the boom. Never describe a plateau as stabilization-is-healthy. (4) Reversal condition is the OPPOSITE event only: a hyperscaler re-ACCELERATING guidance >10% above baseline on a subsequent print. Once fired on a dated print, status persists until the next print.
